stories.title: D11's $775M Bond Measure Is on the November Ballot — What COS Families Need to Know

x_posts.label: Post 1
x_posts.text:
D11 families: $775M bond on the November ballot.

First voter-approved bond since 2004. Repairs at every school, new HVAC, asbestos removal, Coronado AC.

~$260/year for avg homeowner.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
Colorado Springs D11 families, there's something important on the November ballot that affects every family in the district.

On August 5, the D11 Board of Education voted 6-1 to place a $775 million bond measure — Ballot Question 4A — on the November general election ballot. It would be the first voter-approved bond in the district since 2004.

What it covers: repairs at every D11 school. That means new HVAC systems, asbestos removal, modernized classrooms, a full rebuild of one school, and finally getting air conditioning into Coronado High School. The district says the average homeowner would pay approximately $260 per year if the measure passes.

October is the time to get informed before ballots arrive. We'll be covering this one closely in the weeks ahead.

What questions do you have about the D11 bond?

stories.title: Two Squishy Dumpling Toy Lines Recalled Over Deadly Water Bead Hazard — Check Your Kids' Toy Bins

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
CPSC recall: squishy dumpling toys recalled Oct 1.

LLK Trading + ABC Trading (37,000 units) — water beads that expand beyond safe limits.

Ingestion hazard. Stop use now. Refund steps at cpsc.gov/Recalls.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
If your kids have squishy dumpling toys, check the toy bin today.

The CPSC issued two separate recalls on October 1 covering these types of toys. LLK Trading recalled Mochi Malrang Mystery Dumpling Toys — a translucent red squishy dumpling in a bamboo steamer container, sold at Easy Wholesale in San Jose in July for about $10. About 480 units are affected.

ABC Trading recalled around 37,000 Squishy Dumpling Toys (model 3655) and Crazy Squib Ball Toys (model 3984) — multi-color translucent toys with glitter and water beads inside.

Both recalls involve the same hazard: the water beads inside expand beyond the safe limit. If a child swallows one, it can cause choking, intestinal obstruction, severe vomiting, and dehydration — and in serious cases, can be fatal.

Stop use immediately. For each product, write "RECALLED" on the toy and contact the company for a full refund:
- LLK Trading: llktradinginc@gmail.com
- ABC Trading: recallabc@gmail.com

CPSC has now issued five recalls covering about 53,000 of these toys since September 3. This one matters — please share it.

Have you seen either of these toys in your home?

stories.title: D11 Fall Break Is October 19–23 — Activities to Fill the Week

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
D11 fall break: October 19–23 — five school-free days.

Boo at the Zoo runs all month. Garden of the Gods peaks mid-October.

Start planning — two weeks away.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
D11 families — fall break is October 19–23. That's five school-free days starting just two weeks from today.

If you haven't started planning, here's a quick window of what Colorado Springs has going on during that week:

🍂 **Boo at the Zoo** runs all month at Cheyenne Mountain Zoo — kids can trick-or-treat in costume through the zoo, and there's even a haunted house option for bolder kiddos.
🍂 **Garden of the Gods** typically hits peak fall foliage around mid-October, which puts that first week of break right in the sweet spot.
🍂 **Pumpkins in the Park** at Bancroft Park is October 24 — the Saturday immediately after break ends — if you want to close out the week on a free community event.
🍂 **Emma Crawford Coffin Races** in Manitou Springs is also October 24 if your family is up for something uniquely Colorado.

D20 and D49 families: your district calendars likely have similar fall breaks, but check d20.org or d49.org to confirm your exact dates.

stories.title: Halloween in Colorado Springs — Best Family Events in October 2026

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
COS Halloween events for families:

🎃 Oct 22 — Boo at the Bridge, $13, Royal Gorge
🎃 Oct 24 — Pumpkins in the Park, free
🎃 Oct 25 — Halloween Detectives, Pioneers Museum, free
🎃 All month — Boo at the Zoo

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
October in Colorado Springs is genuinely one of the best months of the year — and the Halloween event lineup for families is looking great.

Here's what we're watching for families with kids of all ages:

🎃 **Pumpkins in the Park** (Oct 24, Bancroft Park in Old Colorado City): A free community festival with massive carved pumpkins, live music, and a costume contest. One of the best free family events of the fall season.

🎃 **Boo at the Bridge** (Oct 22, Royal Gorge Bridge, $13): Trick-or-treating, games, and live entertainment at an iconic Colorado backdrop. Kids and parents both tend to love this one.

🎃 **Boo at the Zoo** (ongoing through October 31, Cheyenne Mountain Zoo): Costumed trick-or-treat stations throughout the zoo, plus a haunted house for families who want more of a spooky experience.

🎃 **Halloween History Detectives** (Oct 25, Colorado Springs Pioneers Museum): Trick-or-treating for local history facts plus hands-on crafts. A great option for curious families — and free.

Late October in Colorado Springs typically runs in the upper 50s during the day and drops into the 30s at night, so layers are a must for evening events like Boo at the Zoo or Boo at the Bridge.

stories.title: Parent-Teacher Conference Season Is Here — What to Expect This October

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
PTC season has arrived for COS families.

CIVA Charter: Oct 14–15 and Oct 23–24. D11 has two conference days built into the calendar.

Come prepared with specific questions and take notes.

#COSParenting #ColoradoSprings #COSKids #PikesPeakParenting

facebook.long_form:
It's parent-teacher conference season in Colorado Springs, and the first round of fall PTCs is just around the corner for many families.

CIVA Charter School has conferences scheduled for October 14 (5–7:30 PM, school in session) and October 15 (4–7:30 PM, no school), with a follow-up round on October 23 and 24. D11's school year calendar includes two designated parent-teacher conference days — individual schools typically set specific times and sign-up windows.

If you haven't done a fall PTC in a while, here's what makes them worth preparing for:

- **Come with a question.** Teachers appreciate specificity: "How does my child do with transitions?" goes further than "How are they doing?"
- **Ask what support looks like at home.** Teachers are more likely to have practical suggestions than you'd expect.
- **Ask about the second half of the semester.** Fall PTCs are early enough that there's real time to course-correct before semester grades close.
- **Take notes.** You won't remember everything, and a quick note on your phone is enough.

Check your school's app or website for sign-up windows — many schools open scheduling 1–2 weeks before conferences.
